update_triggers: a key, certificate, trust boundary, or secret consumer changes
a pinned cryptographic dependency or managed provider changes
a security finding or incident affects cryptographic material

included: deployment cryptography protecting application data or access
provider-managed cryptography at the private ingress boundary
test-only cryptographic exceptions that must not reach production
excluded: actual key, password, seed, certificate, hostname, and account values
generic operating-system cryptography not used by the deployment
identity-provider internals outside the household deployment boundary

cryptographic_keys.name: Django signing key
cryptographic_keys.material_type: independent random symmetric key material, at least 50 characters
cryptographic_keys.generation: Generate with an operating-system CSPRNG directly into the protected secret file.
cryptographic_keys.storage: Root-owned deployment secret file; mounted read-only only into approved Django containers.
consumers: Django framework signing for database-backed session payloads
permitted_uses: Django framework signing
domain-separated keyed identifiers that never leave the authenticated application
cryptographic_keys.rotation: Stop ingress and all Django consumers, atomically replace the file, recreate containers, and prove all prior sessions fail.
cryptographic_keys.retirement: Destroy after the replacement is verified; it is not retained because old application signatures must remain invalid.

cryptographic_keys.name: MFA seed-encryption key
cryptographic_keys.material_type: independent random symmetric input key, at least 43 characters
cryptographic_keys.generation: Generate at least 32 random bytes with an operating-system CSPRNG directly into the protected secret file.
cryptographic_keys.storage: Root-owned deployment secret file; mounted read-only only into approved Django consumers.
permitted_uses: derive one domain-separated Fernet key
encrypt and authenticate TOTP seeds at rest
cryptographic_keys.rotation: Use the guarded transaction to decrypt every current-version seed, atomically re-encrypt all seeds under a higher version, and record protected audit events.
cryptographic_keys.retirement: Retain the previous key only in protected recovery custody until rotation and rollback verification finish, then destroy it.

cryptographic_keys.name: Per-user TOTP seeds
cryptographic_keys.generation: Generate 20 random bytes with the Python secrets CSPRNG during enrollment and display only through the authenticated enrollment flow.
cryptographic_keys.storage: Stored only inside authenticated Fernet ciphertext in PostgreSQL; authenticator copies are controlled by each member.
permitted_uses: generate six-digit TOTP authentication codes for the owning account
cryptographic_keys.rotation: Reset MFA after device loss or suspected disclosure, invalidate existing seeds and recovery codes, revoke sessions, and enroll a newly generated seed.
cryptographic_keys.retirement: Delete the encrypted seed and all associated recovery-code hashes during reset; never archive the seed.

cryptographic_keys.name: Audit checkpoint signing key
cryptographic_keys.material_type: independent random HMAC key, generated as 48 random bytes and validated at 32 bytes minimum
cryptographic_keys.generation: Generate with an operating-system CSPRNG directly into an independently protected secret file.
cryptographic_keys.storage: Root-owned secret file mounted read-only only into the integrity container; recovery and retired verification copies stay off-VM.
permitted_uses: authenticate canonical audit checkpoint documents for the matching key ID
prohibited_uses: rewriting historical checkpoints under a new key ID
protected_data: authenticity of external audit checkpoint documents
cryptographic_keys.rotation: Write a final checkpoint under the old key ID, archive that key offline, promote a new key and monotonically new ID, then write and verify a new checkpoint.
cryptographic_keys.retirement: Keep retired keys offline and identified because historical checkpoints require their original key; never remount them into the web container.

cryptographic_keys.name: Restic repository password
cryptographic_keys.material_type: independent random repository unlock password, generated as 48 random bytes
cryptographic_keys.generation: Generate with an operating-system CSPRNG directly into the protected backup secret file.
cryptographic_keys.storage: Root-owned deployment file mounted only into the backup, restore, and key-rotation containers; independent recovery copy stored off-VM.
permitted_uses: derive a Restic repository wrapping key and unlock the repository master keys
prohibited_uses: command-line, environment-variable, log, or source-control transport
cryptographic_keys.rotation: Use Restic key passwd with old and staged password files, verify repository access and integrity, prove the old password fails, then atomically promote the staged file.
cryptographic_keys.retirement: Destroy the old password after the replacement, backup, restore, and recovery copy are verified.

cryptographic_keys.name: Restic repository master encryption and MAC keys
cryptographic_keys.material_type: Restic-generated 256-bit AES key plus 256-bit Poly1305-AES key material
cryptographic_keys.generation: Generated by Restic from its CSPRNG when the repository is initialized.
cryptographic_keys.storage: Wrapped in Restic key files inside the encrypted repository; plaintext exists only inside the networkless backup tooling process while unlocked.
permitted_uses: encrypt and authenticate repository objects
identify and integrity-check repository objects with SHA-256
prohibited_uses: export from Restic into logs or source control
cryptographic_keys.rotation: A password change only rewraps the master keys. Suspected master-key disclosure requires a new repository and complete re-encryption of retained backups.
cryptographic_keys.retirement: Retire the entire old repository only after independently verifying the replacement repository and required retention history.

cryptographic_keys.name: Tailscale node and WireGuard transport keys
cryptographic_keys.owner: Tailscale node administrator and Tailscale client
cryptographic_keys.material_type: per-device Curve25519 node and machine private keys plus ephemeral transport keys
cryptographic_keys.generation: Generated locally by each Tailscale client; reusable enrollment keys are prohibited for this deployment.
cryptographic_keys.storage: Tailscale client state on each approved device and the VM; never mounted into application containers.
consumers: Tailscale clients on approved household devices
Tailscale daemon on the private Linux VM
permitted_uses: authenticate approved tailnet nodes
establish end-to-end encrypted private network transport
protected_data: network traffic between approved Tailscale nodes
cryptographic_keys.rotation: Expire or remove compromised devices in the Tailscale administration plane and enroll the replacement device with a freshly generated node key.
cryptographic_keys.retirement: Remove the node from the tailnet and destroy its local Tailscale state; do not reuse its enrollment identity.

cryptographic_keys.name: Tailscale Serve TLS private key and ACME account key
cryptographic_keys.owner: Tailscale daemon on the private Linux VM
cryptographic_keys.material_type: locally generated private keys for the public-trust TLS certificate and ACME account
cryptographic_keys.generation: Generated locally by Tailscale Serve while provisioning the Let's Encrypt certificate; Tailscale does not receive the private keys.
cryptographic_keys.storage: Tailscale daemon state on the Linux VM; never copied into the repository or application containers.
permitted_uses: authenticate the exact neutral ts.net service hostname and terminate private HTTPS
protected_data: browser-to-private-ingress confidentiality, integrity, and server authentication
cryptographic_keys.rotation: Tailscale Serve renews its managed certificate; each release records the live leaf key algorithm, validity, issuer, and fingerprint only in protected release evidence.
cryptographic_keys.retirement: Disable Serve and remove the node when retiring the hostname; treat any exported private material as compromised and replace it.

cryptographic_keys.name: Linux VM administrator SSH keys
cryptographic_keys.material_type: per-administrator asymmetric SSH keys and VM host keys selected by the hardened host configuration
cryptographic_keys.generation: Generate independently on administrator devices and the VM with current operating-system SSH tooling; password SSH is prohibited.
cryptographic_keys.storage: Private user keys remain on administrator devices; host private keys remain on the VM; only public user keys enter authorized_keys.
permitted_uses: key-only administration over the Tailscale network
cryptographic_keys.rotation: Remove a compromised public key from authorized_keys, replace affected host keys when needed, and verify access from a second approved device before enforcement changes.
cryptographic_keys.retirement: Remove public authorization immediately and securely erase the retired private key from the owning device.

cryptographic_keys.name: PostgreSQL internal certificate-authority private key
cryptographic_keys.material_type: offline ECDSA P-256 certificate-authority private key
cryptographic_keys.generation: Generate with OpenSSL through the guarded PostgreSQL TLS generator in a new mode-0700 authority directory.
cryptographic_keys.storage: Kept only in offline or removable administrator custody; never placed in the deployment secret directory, VM runtime, container, image, environment, log, or repository.
permitted_uses: sign the dedicated PostgreSQL server certificate for the internal db DNS identity
prohibited_uses: presence on the production VM or in an application container
protected_data: trust root for the internal PostgreSQL server identity
cryptographic_keys.rotation: Generate a new CA and server identity in new staging directories, stop database clients, atomically replace all three deployment certificate files, recreate the database and clients, and rerun the production-boundary proof before traffic resumes.
cryptographic_keys.retirement: Retain the prior CA key only in protected offline rollback custody until the replacement deployment is verified, then destroy it.

cryptographic_keys.name: PostgreSQL internal server private key
cryptographic_keys.material_type: ECDSA P-256 private key for the internal db DNS identity
cryptographic_keys.generation: Generate with OpenSSL through the guarded PostgreSQL TLS generator alongside a 397-day server certificate.
cryptographic_keys.storage: Root-owned mode-0440 deployment secret; copied by the root startup wrapper into a mode-0700 tmpfs and changed to PostgreSQL ownership and mode 0600 before the server starts.
permitted_uses: authenticate the PostgreSQL server and establish encrypted internal database TCP sessions
protected_data: confidentiality and integrity of database TCP sessions
cryptographic_keys.rotation: Rotate with a newly generated CA and server identity before the leaf expires, atomically replace the deployment certificate files while clients are stopped, recreate the database and clients, and rerun the production-boundary proof.
cryptographic_keys.retirement: Destroy the prior deployment copy after replacement and rollback verification; the tmpfs copy disappears with the retired database container.

cryptographic_keys.name: PostgreSQL client certificate-authority private key
cryptographic_keys.material_type: offline ECDSA P-256 certificate-authority private key
cryptographic_keys.generation: Generate with OpenSSL through the guarded PostgreSQL TLS generator in the separate mode-0700 authority directory.
cryptographic_keys.storage: Kept only in offline or removable administrator custody; never placed in the deployment secret directory, VM runtime, container, image, environment, log, or repository.
permitted_uses: sign the fixed PostgreSQL service-client identities
prohibited_uses: presence on the production VM or in an application container
protected_data: trust root for production PostgreSQL client authentication
cryptographic_keys.rotation: Generate a new client CA and complete service-client identity set in new staging directories, stop every database client, atomically replace the deployment client CA and all client leaf pairs, recreate PostgreSQL and every client, and rerun the production-boundary proof.
cryptographic_keys.retirement: Retain the prior CA key only in protected offline rollback custody until the replacement deployment is verified, then destroy it.

cryptographic_keys.name: PostgreSQL per-service client private keys
cryptographic_keys.owner: deployment administrator and assigned database client service
cryptographic_keys.material_type: nine unique ECDSA P-256 private keys for fixed production service identities
cryptographic_keys.generation: Generate each key independently with OpenSSL through the guarded PostgreSQL TLS generator alongside its 397-day client certificate.
cryptographic_keys.storage: Each root-owned mode-0440 deployment secret is mounted read-only only into its assigned client container through the dedicated secret-reader group.
permitted_uses: authenticate one fixed service identity to its mapped least-privilege PostgreSQL role
prohibited_uses: authentication as a different service or PostgreSQL role
protected_data: authorization to the mapped PostgreSQL role
cryptographic_keys.rotation: Replace the client authority and all service identities before any leaf expires or immediately after suspected disclosure, recreate affected containers, and rerun the production-boundary proof.
cryptographic_keys.retirement: Destroy retired deployment keys after replacement and rollback verification; never reuse a key for another service identity.

cryptographic_keys.name: Gunicorn server certificate-authority private key
cryptographic_keys.material_type: offline ECDSA P-256 certificate-authority private key
cryptographic_keys.generation: Generate with OpenSSL through the guarded internal TLS generator in a new mode-0700 authority directory.
cryptographic_keys.storage: Kept only in offline or removable administrator custody; never placed in the deployment secret directory, VM runtime, container, image, environment, log, or repository.
permitted_uses: sign the dedicated Gunicorn server certificate for the internal web DNS identity

cryptographic_keys.retirement: Retain the prior CA key only in protected offline rollback custody until the replacement deployment is verified, then destroy it.

cryptographic_keys.name: Gunicorn internal server private key
cryptographic_keys.owner: deployment administrator and Gunicorn web service
cryptographic_keys.material_type: ECDSA P-256 private key for the internal web DNS identity
cryptographic_keys.generation: Generate with OpenSSL through the guarded internal TLS generator alongside a 397-day server certificate.
cryptographic_keys.storage: Root-owned mode-0440 deployment secret mounted read-only only into the Gunicorn web container through the dedicated secret-reader group.
permitted_uses: authenticate Gunicorn and establish encrypted internal HTTP sessions with nginx
prohibited_uses: mounting into nginx or another client
protected_data: confidentiality and integrity of the internal HTTP hop
cryptographic_keys.rotation: Rotate with both internal web authorities and the nginx client identity before the leaf expires, recreate nginx and Gunicorn, and rerun the production-boundary proof.

cryptographic_keys.name: nginx client certificate-authority private key
cryptographic_keys.material_type: offline ECDSA P-256 certificate-authority private key
cryptographic_keys.generation: Generate with OpenSSL through the guarded internal TLS generator in the separate mode-0700 authority directory.
cryptographic_keys.storage: Kept only in offline or removable administrator custody; never placed in the deployment secret directory, VM runtime, container, image, environment, log, or repository.
permitted_uses: sign the sole budget-ingress client identity
prohibited_uses: PostgreSQL, browser, or public TLS issuance
presence on the production VM or in an application container
protected_data: trust root for nginx client authentication to Gunicorn
cryptographic_keys.rotation: Generate a new client CA and nginx identity with the Gunicorn server trust set in new staging directories, stop ingress, atomically replace the six deployment certificate files, recreate nginx and Gunicorn, and rerun the production-boundary proof.
cryptographic_keys.retirement: Retain the prior CA key only in protected offline rollback custody until the replacement deployment is verified, then destroy it.

cryptographic_keys.name: nginx internal client private key
cryptographic_keys.owner: deployment administrator and nginx ingress relay
cryptographic_keys.material_type: ECDSA P-256 private key for the sole budget-ingress client identity
cryptographic_keys.generation: Generate with OpenSSL through the guarded internal TLS generator alongside a 397-day client certificate.

permitted_uses: authenticate the sole nginx relay client to the Gunicorn web service
prohibited_uses: mounting into Gunicorn or another client

cryptographic_keys.rotation: Rotate with both internal web authorities and the Gunicorn server identity before the leaf expires, recreate nginx and Gunicorn, and rerun the production-boundary proof.

algorithms.name: Django PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 password hashing
algorithms.parameters: Django 5.2.17 PBKDF2PasswordHasher, 1,000,000 iterations, random per-value salt; primary production hasher
consumers: dummy hashes used to equalize absent-record work
permitted_uses: one-way password and recovery-code verification

algorithms.name: HMAC-SHA256
algorithms.parameters: Domain-separated messages; keys are purpose-specific except Django-owned signing and keyed-reference uses of its signing key
permitted_uses: keyed authenticity and pseudonymization with the assigned key purpose

algorithms.name: SHA-256
algorithms.parameters: Full 256-bit digest; domain-separated when deriving the MFA Fernet key
consumers: offline corpus provenance and payload integrity
Restic object identifiers and integrity checks
permitted_uses: unkeyed content integrity and identifiers
fixed-length derivation from already random MFA key material

algorithms.name: Fernet version 1 authenticated encryption
algorithms.parameters: 256-bit composite key split into 128-bit AES-CBC encryption and 128-bit HMAC-SHA256 signing keys; random 128-bit IV; PKCS7 padding
permitted_uses: small TOTP seed payloads bound to user ID and key version

algorithms.name: RFC 6238 TOTP with HMAC-SHA1
algorithms.parameters: 160-bit random seed, 30-second step, six digits, one-step clock drift, replay prevention by last accepted step
permitted_uses: TOTP compatibility for possession-factor authentication

algorithms.name: Full SHA-1 digest for offline breached-password membership
algorithms.parameters: Full uppercase 40-hex-character digest; local hash-only corpus; usedforsecurity disabled; no network lookup
permitted_uses: exact compatibility lookup in the reviewed breached-password corpus

algorithms.name: Operating-system cryptographically secure random generator
algorithms.parameters: Python secrets module or OpenSSL rand; requested output length is purpose-specific
consumers: opaque identifiers and test/deployment secret generation
permitted_uses: generate unpredictable keys, codes, nonces, and identifiers
prohibited_uses: non-cryptographic pseudo-random generators for security material

algorithms.name: Restic scrypt repository-key derivation
algorithms.parameters: Parameters and random salt stored in each Restic key file; derives 64 bytes used to unwrap the repository master keys
permitted_uses: derive the Restic repository wrapping key from its independent random repository password

algorithms.name: Restic AES-256-CTR with Poly1305-AES authentication
algorithms.parameters: Restic repository format: random 16-byte nonce, 32-byte AES key, and 32-byte Poly1305-AES key material
permitted_uses: encrypt and authenticate Restic repository objects
prohibited_uses: reuse of repository master keys outside Restic

algorithms.name: Tailscale Serve TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 profile
algorithms.parameters: Go crypto/tls defaults with ECDHE forward secrecy and AEAD selection between AES-128-GCM and ChaCha20-Poly1305; live certificate and negotiation are checked at release
permitted_uses: browser-to-private-ingress HTTPS for the exact ts.net hostname

algorithms.name: PostgreSQL internal mutual TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 profile
algorithms.parameters: PostgreSQL 17 and OpenSSL TLS 1.2 or TLS 1.3 with separate ECDSA P-256 server and client authorities, purpose-bound serverAuth and clientAuth leaves, DNS SAN db, libpq verify-full hostname and exact-CA validation, exact certificate-CN-to-role mapping, and no plaintext or password-authentication fallback
permitted_uses: encrypted, integrity-protected, mutually authenticated PostgreSQL TCP transport on the internal backend network
prohibited_uses: trust outside the dedicated internal CA
password authentication in the production Compose boundary
mapping one service certificate to an unauthorized database role

algorithms.name: Internal nginx-to-Gunicorn mutual TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 profile
algorithms.parameters: nginx and Gunicorn with OpenSSL TLS 1.2 or TLS 1.3, separate ECDSA P-256 server and client authorities, purpose-bound serverAuth and clientAuth leaves, DNS SAN web, exact CA and hostname validation, and no plaintext production listener
permitted_uses: encrypted, integrity-protected, mutually authenticated HTTP transport on the internal frontend network
prohibited_uses: trust outside either dedicated internal web CA
reuse for PostgreSQL, browser, or public TLS
issuing any client identity other than budget-ingress

algorithms.name: Tailscale WireGuard transport suite
algorithms.parameters: Noise_IKpsk2_25519_ChaChaPoly_BLAKE2s using Curve25519, ChaCha20-Poly1305, BLAKE2s, SipHash24, and HKDF
permitted_uses: end-to-end encrypted transport and node authentication inside the tailnet

algorithms.name: Operating-system approved SSH public-key suite
algorithms.parameters: Current hardened OpenSSH client and server policy; exact host and user public-key algorithms are captured during release preflight
permitted_uses: key-only SSH administration over Tailscale

algorithms.name: Django MD5 test password hasher
algorithms.parameters: Django MD5PasswordHasher selected only by config.settings.test
permitted_uses: synthetic local unit-test password fixtures
prohibited_uses: production, hardened, pentest, browser, migration, backup, or release-candidate settings

certificates.name: Private application HTTPS leaf certificate
certificates.owner: Tailscale Serve on the Linux VM
certificates.issuer: Let's Encrypt through Tailscale HTTPS certificate provisioning
certificates.subject: Exact neutral production hostname under the active ts.net tailnet domain; actual hostname is not committed
certificates.key_residency: Generated and stored locally in Tailscale daemon state; never mounted into an application container or received by Tailscale
certificates.validation: Release preflight validates public trust, hostname, validity, TLS 1.2 or 1.3, HSTS, HTTPS-only Serve configuration, and Funnel-disabled state.
certificates.renewal: Managed by Tailscale Serve; Let's Encrypt leaf certificates have a 90-day lifetime. Record the sanitized live issuer, validity, public-key algorithm, and fingerprint per release.

certificates.name: Approved browser public TLS trust roots
certificates.owner: approved device operating system and browser vendor
certificates.subject: Public roots and intermediates required to validate the Tailscale-provisioned Let's Encrypt chain
certificates.key_residency: Root private keys remain with their certificate authorities and are never available to this deployment.
certificates.validation: Current approved browsers must build a valid chain without bypasses; certificate errors fail the release check.
certificates.renewal: Managed through approved-device operating-system and browser updates; stale clients are removed from the tailnet.

certificates.name: PostgreSQL internal certificate-authority certificate
certificates.issuer: Self-issued by the offline Household Budget PostgreSQL authority
certificates.subject: Dedicated internal PostgreSQL authority; actual certificate material is not committed
certificates.key_residency: The public certificate is mounted read-only into approved database clients; its private key remains only in offline administrator custody.
certificates.validation: Every production database client uses libpq verify-full with only this mounted CA file; settings loading and the production-boundary probe fail closed when the certificate or exact trust configuration is absent.
certificates.renewal: Rotate the authority and leaf together before the server leaf expires or immediately after suspected authority compromise, then rerun the production-boundary proof.

certificates.name: PostgreSQL internal server certificate
certificates.issuer: Dedicated offline Household Budget PostgreSQL authority
certificates.subject: Exact internal Docker DNS identity db with matching DNS subject alternative name
certificates.key_residency: The leaf and its private key are root-owned deployment secrets copied into database-only tmpfs; only the public CA certificate reaches clients.
certificates.validation: Generation verifies the leaf chain and at least 30 remaining validity days; every client verifies the exact CA and db hostname, while the runtime probe confirms TLS 1.2 or TLS 1.3 and proves plaintext rejection.
certificates.renewal: The generated leaf lifetime is 397 days. Rotate the complete dedicated authority and server identity in new staging directories before expiration and verify the disposable production boundary before promotion.
prohibited_uses: any DNS identity other than db

certificates.name: PostgreSQL client certificate-authority certificate
certificates.issuer: Self-issued by the offline Household Budget PostgreSQL client authority
certificates.subject: Dedicated PostgreSQL client-authentication authority; actual certificate material is not committed
certificates.key_residency: The public certificate is mounted read-only only into PostgreSQL and copied into database-only tmpfs; its private key remains only in offline administrator custody.
certificates.validation: PostgreSQL uses only this CA to validate client certificates on the cert-authenticated hostssl rule; the production-boundary probe proves an absent client certificate is rejected.
certificates.renewal: Rotate the client authority and all service-client leaves together before any leaf expires or immediately after suspected authority compromise, then rerun the production-boundary proof.

certificates.name: PostgreSQL per-service client certificates
certificates.owner: deployment administrator and assigned database client services
certificates.issuer: Dedicated offline Household Budget PostgreSQL client authority
certificates.subject: Nine fixed service identities mapped to the administrator, migration, runtime, backup, or audit role as narrowly required
certificates.key_residency: Each client leaf and its unique private key are root-owned deployment secrets mounted read-only only into the assigned production service.
certificates.validation: Generation verifies clientAuth purpose and chain; PostgreSQL verifies the client CA and exact CN map, while the runtime proof confirms the web identity and rejects both missing certificates and a web-certificate attempt to assume the audit role.
certificates.renewal: The generated leaf lifetime is 397 days. Rotate the client authority and complete service identity set before expiration, recreate all database clients, and repeat the production-boundary proof.
prohibited_uses: authentication as an unmapped PostgreSQL role
sharing one private key between service identities

certificates.name: Gunicorn server certificate-authority certificate
certificates.owner: deployment administrator and nginx ingress relay
certificates.issuer: Self-issued by the offline Household Budget Gunicorn server authority
certificates.subject: Dedicated internal Gunicorn server authority; actual certificate material is not committed
certificates.key_residency: The public certificate is mounted read-only only into nginx; its private key remains only in offline administrator custody.
certificates.validation: nginx enables proxy certificate verification with only this mounted CA file and verifies the exact web DNS name before sending application traffic.
certificates.renewal: Rotate both internal web authorities and leaves before either leaf expires or immediately after suspected authority compromise, then rerun the production-boundary proof.
prohibited_uses: PostgreSQL, browser, or public TLS trust

certificates.name: Gunicorn internal server certificate
certificates.owner: deployment administrator and Gunicorn web service
certificates.issuer: Dedicated offline Household Budget Gunicorn server authority
certificates.subject: Exact internal Docker DNS identity web with matching DNS subject alternative name
certificates.key_residency: The leaf and private key are root-owned secrets mounted read-only only into Gunicorn; only the public dedicated CA reaches nginx.
certificates.validation: Generation verifies serverAuth purpose, chain, DNS name, and at least 30 remaining validity days; nginx verifies the exact CA and web hostname, while the boundary probe rejects the plaintext port.
certificates.renewal: The generated leaf lifetime is 397 days. Rotate the complete internal web trust set in new staging directories before expiration and verify the disposable production boundary before promotion.
prohibited_uses: any DNS identity other than web

certificates.name: nginx client certificate-authority certificate
certificates.owner: deployment administrator and Gunicorn web service
certificates.issuer: Self-issued by the offline Household Budget nginx client authority
certificates.subject: Dedicated nginx client-authentication authority; actual certificate material is not committed
certificates.key_residency: The public certificate is mounted read-only only into Gunicorn; its private key remains only in offline administrator custody.
certificates.validation: Gunicorn requires a client certificate chained to only this CA on every production connection; no plaintext production listener is configured.
certificates.renewal: Rotate both internal web authorities and leaves before either leaf expires or immediately after suspected authority compromise, then rerun the production-boundary proof.
prohibited_uses: PostgreSQL, browser, or public TLS trust

certificates.name: nginx internal client certificate
certificates.owner: deployment administrator and nginx ingress relay
certificates.issuer: Dedicated offline Household Budget nginx client authority
certificates.subject: Sole purpose-bound client identity budget-ingress
certificates.key_residency: The leaf and its private key are root-owned secrets mounted read-only only into nginx; only the public dedicated client CA reaches Gunicorn.
certificates.validation: Generation verifies clientAuth purpose and chain; Gunicorn requires the dedicated client CA, while the production-boundary proof rejects a connection without the nginx client identity.
certificates.renewal: The generated leaf lifetime is 397 days. Rotate the complete internal web trust set before expiration, recreate nginx and Gunicorn, and repeat the production-boundary proof.
prohibited_uses: sharing the private key with another service

known_absences.current_state: Reusable Tailscale enrollment keys are prohibited and are not part of the deployment.
known_absences.required_action: If automation ever requires enrollment material, inventory it before use, preapprove and narrowly scope it, set a short expiry, and store it outside the checkout.
